SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a festival? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of house
   B. A river
   C. A quiet day
   D. A big celebration

2. Which of these is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A mountain
   B. A clay pot
   C. A river
   D. A cloud

3. Which of these is a traditional drink of the Kalenjin? (1 mark)
   A. Wine
   B. Coffee
   C. Mursik
   D. Cola

4. Which of these is a school value? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating
   B. Stealing
   C. Honesty
   D. Bullying

5. What is discipline? (1 mark)
   A. Running away
   B. Shouting
   C. Doing what you like
   D. Controlling yourself and following rules

6. What does conservation of resources mean? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting resources
   B. Using resources wisely and protecting them
   C. Selling everything at once
   D. Ignoring resources

7. How do economic activities help a county government? (1 mark)
   A. They cause drought
   B. They close clinics
   C. Businesses pay taxes and fees
   D. They stop roads

8. Which is a way of conserving forests? (1 mark)
   A. Building fires
   B. Planting more trees than we cut
   C. Cutting all trees
   D. Burning the forest

9. What is one problem that industries can cause? (1 mark)
   A. Pollution
   B. More rain
   C. Fewer jobs
   D. Less trade

10. Which of these is a benefit of industries? (1 mark)
   A. They close schools
   B. They remove roads
   C. They provide jobs
   D. They stop trade

11. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A tool
   B. A raw material
   C. A worker
   D. A finished good that is made

12. What does the project manager do? (1 mark)
   A. Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   B. Drives the bus
   C. Cooks lunch
   D. Prints books

13. Which is not a good reason to choose a project? (1 mark)
   A. It is safe
   B. It is dangerous but exciting
   C. It is wanted
   D. We have the skills

14. What is income? (1 mark)
   A. Money borrowed
   B. Money spent
   C. Money received from selling
   D. Money lost

15. Which is a benefit of good citizenship in school? (1 mark)
   A. The school is safe and orderly
   B. More fights
   C. Less learning
   D. Property is broken

16. Which of these is a right of a school citizen? (1 mark)
   A. To break rules
   B. To bully others
   C. To steal
   D. To learn in a safe place

17. What does punctuality mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking loudly
   B. Arriving on time
   C. Running fast
   D. Arriving late

18. Why is it important to plan a peace-building activity? (1 mark)
   A. So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   B. So that nobody joins
   C. So that it wastes time
   D. So that it is cancelled

19. Which activity builds peace in school? (1 mark)
   A. A fight
   B. Spreading rumours
   C. A peace poster competition
   D. Cheating

20. If you see a pupil being bullied, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore
   B. Laugh
   C. Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   D. Join in

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give four school rules and one reason for each. (4 marks)

22. Explain why discipline is important in school. (3 marks)

23. Name the six aspects of traditional culture. (3 marks)

24. List four questions you could ask to find out the history of your school. (4 marks)

25. Describe the houses of two communities in Kenya. (4 marks)

26. Give three school values and say why each is important. (3 marks)

27. Explain how good citizenship in school prepares pupils to be good citizens of Kenya. (4 marks)

28. Explain what a raw material is and give one example. (2 marks)

29. Describe how a pupil can help a new pupil to settle in. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — A big celebration
   Festivals are big celebrations with songs and dances.

2. B — A clay pot
   A clay pot is made by people.

3. C — Mursik
   Mursik is fermented milk.

4. C — Honesty
   Honesty is a positive value.

5. D — Controlling yourself and following rules
   Discipline is self-control and obeying rules.

6. B — Using resources wisely and protecting them
   Conservation keeps resources for the future.

7. C — Businesses pay taxes and fees
   Taxes and fees help pay for services.

8. B — Planting more trees than we cut
   Replanting keeps the forest alive.

9. A — Pollution
   Waste from factories can pollute air and water.

10. C — They provide jobs
   Industries employ people.

11. D — A finished good that is made
   Products are the goods that come out of a factory.

12. A — Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   The manager coordinates the work.

13. B — It is dangerous but exciting
   A project must be safe for children.

14. C — Money received from selling
   Income is what you receive from sales.

15. A — The school is safe and orderly
   Good citizens make a peaceful school.

16. D — To learn in a safe place
   Learning safely is a right.

17. B — Arriving on time
   Punctual people arrive on time.

18. A — So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   Planning helps activities succeed.

19. C — A peace poster competition
   Competitions on peace teach and encourage it.

20. C — Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   Reporting helps to stop bullying.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Come on time to avoid missing lessons; keep the school clean for health; respect others for peace; care for property so it lasts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule with a reason.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the school orderly, it helps everyone learn, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, and festivals and ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, 1 mark for two or three.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: When was the school started? Who started it? Who was the first headteacher? How has the school changed?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each relevant question.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: The Maasai build low houses of wooden frames covered with mud and dung inside a fence called a manyatta. Old coastal houses in Lamu were built of coral stone with carved doors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each community and 1 mark for each description.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty helps us to be trusted. Respect keeps peace. Responsibility helps us to do our duties. Accept other valid values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each value with a reason.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Pupils learn to follow rules, respect others, take care of public property and take responsibility. These habits continue when they are adults.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: A raw material is a material used to make something new, for example sugarcane used to make sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Welcome the pupil, show the classrooms and toilets, and invite the pupil to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.
